hook: What if the Sun vanished right now?

blocks.narration: What if the Sun vanished right now? For eight minutes, you would not notice anything at all. Here is why.
blocks.visual: A glowing clay Sun suddenly shrinking to a tiny spark against a deep starry clay sky, a small blue Earth watching

blocks.narration: Sunlight takes about eight minutes and twenty seconds to reach Earth, so the light already on its way keeps arriving.
Gravity changes also travel at the speed of light, so Earth would keep circling an empty spot for those same minutes.
blocks.visual: A clay Earth on a glowing orbit line circling an empty dark spot where the Sun used to be

blocks.narration: Then the sky goes dark and Earth flies off in a straight line. Plants stop making food from sunlight almost immediately.
The oceans would hold heat for a while, but the cold would win. Follow for more what-ifs about space.
blocks.visual: A clay ocean slowly freezing over under a black starry sky, a faint glow fading from the water

cta: Follow for more what-ifs about space.

captions.hook_line: What if the Sun vanished right now? You'd have 8 minutes and not even know ☀️
captions.body: Sunlight takes about 8 minutes 20 seconds to reach Earth, and changes in gravity travel at the speed of light too, so for those minutes nothing would seem to change.
captions.share_line: Send this to someone who loves space what-ifs.
